claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for release because current aggregate readiness passes, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and policy permits certification if the current telehealth discharge planning weakness is explicitly disclosed in current release documentation or covered by approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness passing and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness but are not alone sufficient for certification under the stated policy.
A current material segment weakness for a named launch use case triggers a mandatory condition: disclosure in current release documentation unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Contextual items such as prior approvals and informal monitoring notes cannot substitute for current evidence of disclosure or reviewed mitigation.
Because the actor's conclusion depends on a policy predicate not proven by the admissible record, the claim is not fully supported even though it is directionally plausible.
evidence_requests: The current release documentation or model-card text showing the telehealth discharge planning limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Any approved risk acceptance, mitigation approval, or sign-off covering the current subgroup regression before launch.
The final certification packet demonstrating that current evaluation results, including the subgroup regression, are reflected in the release documentation.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold is conditional: certification is allowed only if the current release documentation actually discloses the material weakness or there is approved risk acceptance, and no admissible evidence shows either condition is satisfied.

The telehealth discharge planning slice is a current regression below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which makes the disclosure or approved-mitigation predicate material rather than optional.
The release-thread monitoring comment is explicitly unsupported by reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language, so it cannot close the policy gap.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it does not support current certification beyond background context.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently compliant on the existing record, rather than merely potentially supportable if disclosure is added before launch.
That the model-card materials already contain the required current telehealth discharge limitation disclosure.
That any approved risk acceptance exists for the current subgroup regression.
